analysis.title: GS - Jeter - Earnings Recap - 27 Oct 2026
key_insights: CLS: Beat and raise with a buyback. 3Q26 EBIAT $496 mn (8.5% margin) vs GS/consensus $450/$451 mn on revenue of $5.83 bn, gross margin of 11.2% missed. 4Q26 revenue beat the midpoint by $430 mn and 2026E revenue guidance was raised by $500 mn. FCF guidance cut to $460 mn from $600 mn. Stock +15% pre-market, with an 8am ET call and Investor Day.

CLS initial 2027 outlook: revenue $40.0 bn (GS/consensus $39.0/$34.9 bn), EBIAT margin 9.0% (8.7%/8.6%), EPS $21.50 (GS $20.83, consensus $19.24). Capex of $1.5-$2.0 bn implies roughly breakeven FCF by GS estimate. A 2.5% of public float NCIB (the TSX equivalent of a buyback authorization) was announced.

CDNS: Results in line with the Street, 2026 guidance raised. Revenue $1.63 bn vs $1.62 bn, non-GAAP EPS $2.11 vs $2.05, IP revenue $245 mn vs GS $229 mn and Street $235 mn. 2026 revenue guided to a $6.402 bn midpoint (Street $6.33 bn), EPS $8.40 midpoint (Street $8.16). Agentic AI tools are expected to raise consumption of the underlying EDA tools, and the agent layer uses a consumption-plus-subscription model. Stock +2% pre-market.

Industrials: strong order and backlog prints at JCI (Q4 orders +44% organically, backlog $23 bn, +43% y/y), INIO (backlog $8 bn, +142% y/y, 2026 outlook raised) and HRI (EPS $3.91 vs $2.99, full-year EBITDA guide raised to $2.10-2.15 bn). UPS beat and raised revenue guidance, but the SCF segment missed on EBIT.

Industrials misses and guide-downs: XYL cut FY EPS to $5.40-$5.45 and guided organic revenue growth to 0% vs consensus +2.32%. GBX guided 2027 EBIT margin of 7-7.5% vs 10% consensus. WSO, AWI, ABG, SHW and CLW missed EPS. AIT and PNR beat but PNR's Q4 EPS guide of $1.15 was below the $1.21 consensus.
Tariff refunds boosted results at PII (about $1.09 of FY EPS) and PNR ($8mm of IEEPA refunds in the quarter). PII raised full-year guidance for the third time this year.

Financials: SPGI beat on Indices, ramped up buybacks ($2.6 bn in 3Q, more than $3 bn expected in 4Q) and opened a strategic review of possible separation of Capital IQ and associated data businesses. TRU beat on EPS, but its 4Q guide was below the Bloomberg EPS figure of $1.19, with mortgage inquiries expected to fall 20%+. SOFI beat and raised with a 2027 EPS guide about 10% above the Street.

Financials, mixed: HIG beat on operating EPS ($3.50 vs $3.13) but Middle & Large Commercial underlying combined ratio worsened 8pp y/y to 99.5%, making its ~92.3% full-year guide hard to meet. BRO missed on Specialty Distribution organic growth of -0.8%. PYPL branded checkout grew 1% and its quality of beat was questioned, with focus on any strategic update.

Consumer: RCL raised FY EPS to $17.85-$17.95 and gave a 2027 EPS framework with a $20 handle (consensus $20.32). 4Q net yields are expected to inflect to the mid-4% range. HLT guided 4Q EPS below consensus, citing midterms and the Middle East as RevPAR headwinds, and positioning was long going in. KO beat on organic revenue (+7% vs +4.4%) with North America the only soft region.

Consumer weakness: SMPL guided Q1 sales -19% to -22% and FY27 sales -13% to -17%, far below consensus. WHR printed 3Q EPS of -$0.21 vs $0.73 consensus, cut 2026 sales and adjusted EBIT margin guides, and now sees FY adjusted EPS of -$1.30. SFD missed on EPS and sales on soft pork and packaged meats.

Healthcare: HCA beat on adjusted EBITDA ($3.92 bn vs $3.73 bn) and expects results in the upper half of its 2026 guidance range, but a payer mix shift toward uninsured volume cost about $400 million of pre-tax income in 3Q. CNC raised EPS guidance to above $5.20 on revenue of $50.7 bn vs $47 bn consensus, with Marketplace MBR missing by 190 bps. IQV, RGEN and NVO were modestly ahead.
Implied moves quoted for the post-earnings sessions: INIO 16%, HRI 9%, GBX 9%, JCI 6%, UPS 6%, ABG 6%, AWI 6%, LECO 5%, BA 5%, AIT 4%, SHW 2%.

BA: Q3 free cash flow $464mm vs $325mm consensus, revenue $24.2bn in line, headline EPS loss wider than expected. 777x first delivery remains on track for 2027 and 737 production is heading to a stabilized 47 per month.
Utilities and materials were in line: CMS reaffirmed FY26 and FY27 EPS ranges and 6-8% long-term growth. NUE had EPS a touch better than consensus and returned $629mn to shareholders.

earnings_insights: CLS: 3Q26 EBIAT $496 mn reported vs GS $450 mn / consensus (Visible Alpha) $451 mn, revenue $5.83 bn reported, gross margin 11.2% reported and a miss. 2027E guidance (company outlook, not yet reported): revenue $40.0 bn vs GS/consensus $39.0/$34.9 bn, EBIAT margin 9.0%, EPS $21.50 vs GS/consensus $20.83/$19.24.

CDNS: revenue $1.63 bn reported vs GS/Street $1.62 bn, operating margin 44.1% reported vs 44.2% estimate, non-GAAP EPS (excl. SBC) $2.11 reported vs $2.05 estimate. 2026 guidance midpoints: revenue $6.402 bn, operating margin 44.7%, EPS $8.40 vs prior $8.05-$8.15.
JCI: Q4 EPS $1.66 reported vs $1.59 consensus, sales $7.1bn vs $7.04bn consensus. Q1 guide $1.15-1.20 vs $1.13 consensus and fiscal 2027 EPS guide $6.15-6.30 vs $6.15 consensus.

JBLU: Q3 revenue $2.81bn reported vs $2.83bn consensus. The note prints EPS as (40.60) vs consensus ($0.54), apparently a loss of about $0.60 vs a $0.54 loss expected. FY26 RASM guide 13.5-14.5% vs 13.2% consensus.
HRI: Q3 EPS $3.91 reported vs $2.99 consensus, revenue $1.36bn vs $1.33bn, EBITDA $603mm vs $583mm. FY EBITDA guide $2.10-2.15bn vs $2.05-2.13bn prior.
INIO: Q3 sales $1.2bn reported vs $1.05bn consensus, EPS $0.15 vs $0.12, EBITDA $245mm vs $198mm. FY26 revenue outlook raised by $100mm to $3.9-4bn and EBITDA outlook to $780-800mm.

UPS: Q3 EPS $1.69 reported vs $1.63 consensus, sales $22.9bn vs $22.3bn. FY EPS $7.28 vs $7.19 consensus and FY revenue guide $92.6bn from $91.2bn. SCF EBIT $274mm vs $296mm consensus, International EBIT $746mm vs $676mm.
LECO: Q3 EPS $2.98 reported vs $2.81 consensus, sales $1.22bn vs $1.17bn, EBIT $220mm vs $210mm.
BA: Q3 free cash flow $464mm reported vs $325mm consensus, revenue $24.2bn vs $23.9bn, headline EPS loss of 34c vs a 20c loss expected.
ABG: Q3 EPS $6.16 reported vs $6.42 consensus, gross profit $732mm vs $746mm. Same-store new vehicle revenue down 8%.
CMS: Q3 EPS $1.44 reported vs $1.35 consensus, revenue $2.18bn vs $2.23bn. FY26 EPS guide $3.83-$3.90 vs $3.87 consensus and FY27 $4.08-$4.17 vs $4.15.
AIT: fiscal Q1 EPS $2.97 reported vs $2.89 consensus on sales of $1.29bn in line. FY EPS guide $11.70-12.20 vs $11.65-12.15 prior.
PNR: Q3 EPS $1.18 reported vs $1.07 consensus including $8mm of IEEPA refunds, sales $976mm vs $964mm. Q4 EPS guide $1.15 vs $1.21 consensus, FY EPS $4.70.
GBX: Q4 EPS $0.39 reported vs $0.80 consensus, revenue $591mm vs $605mm. 2027 revenue guide $2.8-3.2bn vs $2.7bn consensus and EBIT margin 7-7.5% vs 10% consensus.
XYL: 3Q EPS $1.44 reported vs $1.45 consensus, revenue below $2.20bn vs $2.28bn consensus, adjusted EBITDA $527mn vs $544.3mn. FY EPS guide cut to $5.40-$5.45 from $5.55-$5.70.
HUBB: 3Q adjusted EPS $5.91 reported vs $5.76 consensus, revenue $1.87bn vs $1.85bn. FY adjusted EPS guide $20.40-$20.60 vs $20.25-$20.55 prior.
SHW: Q3 EPS $3.63 reported vs $3.69 consensus, sales $6.86bn vs $6.78bn. FY guide narrowed to $11.85-12.15 with the same midpoint.
WSO: Q3 EPS $3.77 reported vs $4.10 consensus, revenue $2.22bn vs $2.21bn, EBIT $225mm vs $245mm.
AWI: Q3 EPS $2.26 reported vs $2.39 consensus, EBITDA $164mm vs $170mm. Full-year EBITDA guide $602-612mm vs $605-620mm prior.
CLW: Q3 sales $385mm reported vs $392mm consensus, EBITDA $24mm vs $25mm. The note prints EPS as ($0.23) vs consensus (40.14), apparently a $0.14 loss expected.
NE: revenue beat but adjusted EBITDA light. Low end of FY revenue guidance raised and high end of FY adjusted EBITDA guidance lowered.
TRU: EPS $1.25 reported vs $1.20 consensus, organic revenue growth 8.0%, EBITDA margin 35.4%. 4Q adjusted EPS guide $1.15-1.22 vs Bloomberg consensus $1.19.

SPGI: headline earnings beat on Indices, Market Intelligence organic constant-currency growth 7.0% reported with a 36.2% margin. Buyback $2.6bn in 3Q and $4bn YTD, with more than $7bn expected for FY.
SOFI: beat and raise with a 2027 EPS guide about 10% above the Street. Origination beat came from personal lending, more than 20 percentage points above consensus.
IVZ: operating income $562mn reported, about 5% better, with revenue largely in line. Fee rate 21.5bps vs 22.4bps in 2Q.
BRX: FFO of 60c reported, 1c above the street, FY26 FFO range raised by 1c on both ends. Billed occupancy 91.4%.
AB: net revenues $904mn reported in line, fee rate 36.9bps vs 37.2bps street, operating margin 33.5% in line.
HIG: operating EPS $3.50 reported vs $3.13 street, P&C catastrophe losses 4.2% vs 5.2% street. P&C and Employee Benefits net written/earned premium growth +4% vs +3% street.
BRO: adjusted EPS $1.07 reported, 3c below consensus, on a 2pp total revenue miss. Adjusted EBITDAC margin beat by 30bps.

RCL: 3Q EPS $6.57 reported vs $6.38 consensus, net yields +0.6%. FY EPS guide raised to $17.85-$17.95 vs $17.79 consensus, 4Q EPS guide $3.48-$3.58 vs $3.65 consensus. 2027 EPS framework at a $20 handle vs $20.32 consensus.
PII: Q3 EPS $1.08 ex-items reported vs $0.59 consensus, including $0.13 of tariff refunds. Revenue $2.04B vs $1.90B. FY EPS guide $3.50-3.60 vs $3.14 consensus.
KO: 3Q EPS $0.91 reported vs $0.88 consensus, organic revenue +7% vs +4.4% consensus. North America +3% vs +4% consensus, LatAm +16% vs +7%.
SFD: adjusted EPS $0.26 reported vs $0.33 estimate, sales $3.44bn vs $3.69bn estimate.
HLT: Q3 EPS $2.45 ex-items reported vs $2.37 consensus, revenue $3.33B vs $3.37B. Q4 EPS guide $2.32-2.38 vs $2.39 consensus. FY EPS guide $9.07-9.13 vs $9.06 consensus.
SMPL: Q4 EPS $0.44 ex-items reported vs $0.40 consensus, revenue $333.3M vs $327.1M. Q1 sales guide -19% to -22% vs -12.2% consensus and FY27 sales guide -13% to -17% vs -8.7% consensus.
WHR: 3Q EPS -$0.21 ex-items reported vs $0.73 consensus, revenue $3.68B vs $3.93B, EBIT $97M vs $183M. FY adjusted EPS outlook cut to -$1.30 vs $1.21 consensus.
HCA: Q3 revenue $19.85B reported vs $19.33B estimate, adjusted EBITDA $3.92B vs $3.73B estimate. Payer mix shift estimated to cut pre-tax income by about $400 million in the quarter.
IQV: 3Q revenue $4.43B reported vs $4.37B consensus, adjusted EBITDA $1.03B vs $1.01B. FY EBITDA guide $4.025B to $4.055B vs $4B to $4.05B prior.
RGEN: 3Q revenue $209M reported vs $207M consensus, EPS $0.53 vs $0.46. EPS guide $2.05 to $2.09 vs $2.03 to $2.09 prior.
CNC: 3Q revenue $50.7B reported vs $47B consensus, EPS $0.58 vs $0.10 consensus. FY EPS guide raised to greater than $5.20 from greater than $4.80.
NVO: 3Q26 core operating profit beat of 8%, net sales broadly in line, COGS 2% below consensus, SG&A 10% below and R&D 4% below.
risk_factors: SOFI: strength in origination activity used capital (-180bps QoQ), so capital intensity and runway are likely bear focus points.
HIG: workers' compensation and non-cat weather deterioration in Middle & Large Commercial, plus pressure in Group Disability, may threaten margin guidance.
BRO: continued declines in CAT/DIC property rates and some further moderation in retail pricing through the rest of 2026.
HCA: payer mix shift toward uninsured volume after patients lost coverage on the health insurance exchanges.
WHR: weak housing, lower consumer confidence and rising freight and raw material costs are expected to persist.
CLS: FCF guide cut to $460 mn and 2027 capex of $1.5-$2.0 bn implies about breakeven FCF, with possible capital raising implications.
SMPL: significant 2027 declines in net sales and adjusted EBITDA as pricing volume effects work through.
SFD: softer fresh pork and hog commodity markets.
vol_and_positioning: Implied post-earnings moves quoted: INIO 16%, HRI 9%, GBX 9%, JCI 6%, UPS 6%, ABG 6%, AWI 6%, LECO 5%, BA 5%, AIT 4%, SHW 2%.
UPS stock is down the last two prints and on 13 of 18 prints.
HLT positioning was long going into the print, which weighed on the reaction to the weaker Q4 guide.
SPGI is ramping its buyback to more than $7bn for FY, and CLS announced an NCIB of 2.5% of public float.
geopolitical: HLT flagged the Middle East and midterms as headwinds to Q4 RevPAR growth.
IEEPA tariff refunds boosted quarterly results at PNR ($8mm) and PII (about $1.09 of FY EPS across Q2 and Q3).
